Office of Information and GIS Services
The Delaware County Office of Information and GIS Services manages the County’s Geographic Information System (GIS) and serves as the central point of contact for Delaware County’s web-based applications and mapping services, as well as provides video streaming coordination and services for county government meetings.
Our department creates, maintains, and provides access to the County’s GIS databases and mapping resources. These tools support County departments, partner agencies, and the public by providing reliable geographic information and interactive mapping applications.
The Office of Information and GIS Services also actively supports the Delaware County Emergency Management Agency and 911 Communications Center and is co-located in the Emergency Operations Center. In this role, our staff members are designated as responding units and provides technical support, logistics coordination, planning assistance, and mapping support during emergency preparedness, response, and recovery operations.
The Office of Information also serves as the primary administrator of the county website, providing management, maintenance, and technical support and training to all the departments that maintain content on the site.
Publicly accessible data and online maps
We work to make County data accessible and easy to use. Many of the maps and datasets we maintain are available through online applications that allow residents, businesses, and partner agencies to explore geographic information. Visit our ArcGIS Online site to view the online maps and applications we make available.
Downloadable GIS datasets are also available through the County’s Open Data portal.
Visit the Delaware County Open Data Portal: https://maps-delcogis.opendata.arcgis.com
The Open Data portal allows users to view, explore, and download selected datasets maintained by Delaware County.
Note: This data requires specialized GIS Software to view.
What is GIS?
A Geographic Information System (GIS) is a computer-based system used to create, manage, analyze, and display geographic information.
GIS connects data to real-world locations, allowing organizations to visualize information on maps and better understand relationships between places, infrastructure, and services.
Examples of information managed in a GIS include:
Property and parcel boundaries
Roads and transportation networks
Utilities and infrastructure
Environmental features
Public facilities and services
Emergency response resources
By organizing information geographically, GIS helps government agencies make informed decisions and deliver services more efficiently.
Our mission and goals
The Delaware County Office of Information and GIS Services has three primary goals.
Maintain accurate geographic data
Develop and maintain a modern GIS that provides accurate and comprehensive geographic information about Delaware County.
Provide access to data
Deliver GIS data, mapping applications, and geographic information to residents, businesses, partner organizations, and government agencies.
Support County operations
Provide professional GIS consulting, analysis, and application development to support County departments and partner agencies.
County GIS data
The foundation of Delaware County’s GIS is a collection of geographic datasets known as GIS data layers .
These layers represent many aspects of the County, including:
Property and parcel information
Transportation networks and roads
Public Infrastructure
Environmental and natural features
Parks and recreational facilities
Government buildings and services
Emergency services locations and response resources
GIS data layers are developed and maintained by the Office of Information and GIS Services in partnership with other County departments using ESRI’s ArcGIS mapping platform.
How GIS supports county departments
Delaware County operates an Enterprise GIS , meaning that mapping technology is integrated into the daily work of multiple County departments and partner organizations.
GIS tools help agencies:
Improve efficiency and reduce operational costs
Analyze data more effectively
Support planning and infrastructure management
Enhance public safety and emergency response
Improve data-driven decision making
To support these efforts, the Office of Information and GIS Services provides consulting and technical support to County departments and partner organizations. We work with agencies to identify opportunities where GIS can improve workflows, streamline operations, and enhance public services.
When appropriate, our office may also develop custom GIS applications designed to meet the operational needs of County departments and partner agencies.
